source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An adult with a protruding jaw, enlarged hands, and coarse features likely has:
questions.rationale: Acromegaly: GH excess after epiphyseal closure, causing bone and soft tissue enlargement without height gain.
questions.quote: An excess of Growth hormone in adults

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, clear nasal drainage should be tested for:
questions.rationale: Glucose in nasal drainage indicates CSF leak.
questions.quote: Observe for post-nasal drip and check for glucose

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which complication after hypophysectomy causes large volumes of dilute urine?
questions.rationale: Transient DI may follow pituitary surgery.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acromegaly Nursing Management (PDF p. 360)
questions.quote: Transient diabetes insipidus

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After hypophysectomy, the client should avoid:
questions.rationale: Avoid activities that raise ICP; keep HOB elevated; deep breathing (not coughing) is taught.
questions.quote: Patient is cautioned against engaging in activities that increases ICP

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Amenorrhea and galactorrhea in a nonpregnant woman suggest:
questions.rationale: Prolactin-secreting tumors cause amenorrhea and galactorrhea.
questions.quote: Galactorrhea

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with lung cancer has low sodium, concentrated urine, and weight gain. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Bronchogenic carcinoma can cause SIADH with dilutional hyponatremia.
questions.quote: Bronchogenic carcinoma

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the key nursing intervention for SIADH?
questions.rationale: Restrict fluids; monitor weight, I&O, sodium, and neuro status.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, SIADH Management (PDF p. 362)
questions.quote: Restrict fluid intake as indicated

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which urine specific gravity is typical of diabetes insipidus?
questions.rationale: DI produces very dilute urine (SG 1.001–1.005).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Diabetes Insipidus (PDF p. 362)
questions.quote: Dilute urine with a specific gravity of 1.001 to 1.005

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug treats central diabetes insipidus?
questions.rationale: DDAVP is synthetic vasopressin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DI Management (PDF p. 362)
questions.quote: Desmopressin (DDAVP)- intranasal synthetic vasopressin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which test differentiates central from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus?
questions.rationale: Kidneys concentrate urine after ADH in central DI, not in nephrogenic DI.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DI Diagnostics (PDF p. 362)
questions.quote: differentiates central from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the most common cause of endemic goiter?
questions.rationale: Endemic (simple) goiter results from iodine deficiency; prevented by iodized salt (RA 8172, ASIN Law).
questions.quote: Caused by iodine deficiency

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding is typical of Graves' disease?
questions.rationale: Hyperthyroidism: exophthalmos, heat intolerance, weight loss, tachycardia.
questions.quote: Bulging eyes, which produces a startled facial expression

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Lid lag when the client looks downward is called:
questions.rationale: von Graefe's: lid lag; Dalrymple's: upper lid retraction.
questions.quote: von Graefe’s sign: eyelid lag when looking downwards

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on propylthiouracil develops sore throat and fever. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Agranulocytosis is the most toxic effect; stop and get hematologic studies.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Antithyroid Medications (PDF p. 364)
questions.quote: Agranulocytosis is the most toxic side effects.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should Lugol's solution be given?
questions.rationale: Mix in milk or juice and use a straw to prevent teeth staining.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Adjunctive Therapy (PDF p. 364)
questions.quote: Administer through a straw to prevent staining of the teeth

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is iodine (Lugol's) given before thyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: Iodine decreases hormone release and thyroid vascularity, reducing blood loss.
questions.quote: Iodine (Lugol’s solution or KI) may be prescribed in an effort to reduce blood loss

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding indicates iodism?
questions.rationale: Iodism: buccal swelling, salivation, coryza, skin eruptions.
questions.quote: Excessive Salivation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which environment suits a client with hyperthyroidism?
questions.rationale: Keep the room cool, quiet, uncluttered; use calm approach.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperthyroidism Nursing (PDF p. 365)
questions.quote: Maintain the environment at a cool, comfortable temperature

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet suits a client with hyperthyroidism?
questions.rationale: Hypermetabolism requires high calories and protein; avoid stimulants and spices.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperthyroidism Nursing (PDF p. 364)
questions.quote: High calorie, high protein foods are encouraged

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Cold intolerance, weight gain, bradycardia, and dry skin suggest:
questions.rationale: Hypothyroidism slows metabolism.
questions.quote: Cold intolerance

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why are sedatives given cautiously to a client with hypothyroidism?
questions.rationale: Analgesics, sedatives, and anesthetics have prolonged effects; risk of myxedema coma.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothyroidism Management (PDF p. 365)
questions.quote: the effects of analgesic agents, sedatives, and anesthetic agents are prolonged

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When starting levothyroxine in an older client with CAD, the nurse monitors for:
questions.rationale: Thyroid replacement increases oxygen demand; watch for angina and dysrhythmias.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothyroidism Management (PDF p. 365)
questions.quote: Angina or dysrhythmias can occur.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Hyperparathyroidism commonly causes:
questions.rationale: Excess PTH causes hypercalcemia, renal calculi, bone pain, fractures.
questions.quote: Renal stones
